name: Guwahati
description: Guwahati is the largest city in Assam and the main gateway to the entire Northeast. Situated on the banks of the Brahmaputra, it is home to the Kamakhya Temple, one of the most sacred Shakti peethas in India. The city serves as an excellent base for exploring Assam and beyond.
top_highlights: Umananda Island — smallest inhabited river island
how_to_reach_budget: Fly to Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi Airport (GAU). Shared sumo/bus to Shillong ₹200-300. Local buses within city ₹10-20. Prepaid autos ₹100-200.
how_to_reach_private: Hire private cab from airport (₹600-800 city drop). Ola/Uber available. Drive to Kaziranga (NH27, 4-5 hrs).
entry_fees: Kamakhya Temple: free; Umananda ferry: ₹25 return; Assam State Museum: ₹10
permit_info: No permit required for Indian citizens.
cultural_etiquette: Remove footwear at temples. Photography restricted inside Kamakhya sanctum. Dress modestly.

name: Shillong
description: Shillong is the charming capital of Meghalaya, known for its cool climate, colonial-era architecture, vibrant music scene, and proximity to Cherrapunji and the living root bridges. Ward's Lake and Police Bazar are the city's hubs.
top_highlights: Police Bazar — street shopping and food
how_to_reach_budget: Shared sumo from Guwahati: ₹200-300, 2.5-3 hrs. Sumo stand at Paltan Bazar, Guwahati. Local city taxis ₹100-200.
how_to_reach_private: Private cab from Guwahati ₹1500-2000. NH6 route via Nongpoh.
entry_fees: Ward's Lake: ₹10; Police Bazar: free; Don Bosco Museum: ₹100
cultural_etiquette: Meghalaya is matrilineal; respect Khasi customs. Music is part of local culture — enjoy responsibly.

name: Cherrapunji (Sohra)
tagline: Wettest Place on Earth — Waterfalls and Clouds
best_season: October to April (best waterfalls in June-Sep but risky roads)
description: Cherrapunji, locally known as Sohra, holds the record for most rainfall in a calendar year. It is ringed by spectacular waterfalls — Nohkalikai (India's tallest at 340m), Seven Sisters Falls — and offers the starting trail for Nongriat root bridges. Views over the Bangladesh plains are breathtaking.
top_highlights: Nohkalikai Falls — India's tallest plunge waterfall (340m)
Eco Park panoramic views over Bangladesh
Starting point for Nongriat root bridge trek
how_to_reach_budget: Shared sumo from Shillong to Cherrapunji: ₹100-150, 1.5-2 hrs from Anjali cinema stand. No direct AC bus.
entry_fees: Eco Park: ₹30; Mawsmai Cave: ₹20; Nohkalikai viewpoint: free
permit_info: No permit needed. Standard Meghalaya entry.
cultural_etiquette: Sohra is a Khasi community. Carry your own water (expensive locally). Support local homestays.

name: Nongriat — Living Root Bridges
tagline: Trek to India's Living Engineering Marvel
description: Nongriat is a remote Khasi village accessible only on foot via 3,500+ stone steps from Tyrna. It hosts the Double Decker Living Root Bridge — a Khasi engineering marvel grown over 500 years from rubber tree roots. Staying overnight gives access to Rainbow Falls and a serene jungle experience.
top_highlights: Double Decker Living Root Bridge — 500-year-old bio-engineering
Rainbow Falls — 2 hr trek from root bridges
Natural swimming pools in crystal-clear streams
how_to_reach_budget: Shared sumo/auto to Tyrna village (₹50-80 from Cherrapunji). Then 3,500 steps down on foot (1.5-2 hrs). No vehicles beyond Tyrna.
how_to_reach_private: Private cab to Tyrna trailhead ₹400-600. Trek is mandatory.
entry_fees: Village entry fee: ₹50 per person (collected at top of steps)
permit_info: No formal permit. Village entry fee collected locally.
cultural_etiquette: This is a living village. Ask before photographing residents. Don't litter — carry all trash back up. Book homestays in advance (call ahead — no cell signal in village).
emergency_contact: No cell signal in village. Nearest help at Tyrna or Cherrapunji. Emergency: pre-arrange with homestay owner.

name: Dawki & Shnongpdeng
tagline: India's Clearest River — Boats on Glass
description: Dawki sits on the Indo-Bangladesh border on the turquoise Umngot River. Boats appear to float on air because the water is so clear. Nearby Shnongpdeng is the adventure hub: camping on the riverbank, kayaking, snorkelling, cliff jumping, and zip-lining. Viral photos here every winter.
top_highlights: Umngot River boat rides — glass-bottom effect
Shnongpdeng adventure sports: kayaking, cliff jump, zip-line
how_to_reach_budget: Shared sumo from Shillong to Dawki: ₹150-200, 3-4 hrs. From Cherrapunji hire local cab ₹700-900 to Dawki.
how_to_reach_private: Private cab from Shillong ₹2500-3000 day trip.
entry_fees: Boat rides: ₹500-800 per boat (up to 5 pax); Adventure at Shnongpdeng: ₹300-800 per activity
permit_info: Bangladesh border area — do not cross. Indian citizens: no permit. Carry photo ID.
cultural_etiquette: This is a border area — no photography toward Bangladesh side without guidance. Respect local fishing communities. Camp only at designated Shnongpdeng spots.

name: Mawlynnong — Asia's Cleanest Village
tagline: Asia's Cleanest Village — Khasi Community Pride
description: Mawlynnong won 'Asia's Cleanest Village' in 2003 and has maintained standards since. The village has immaculate paths lined with flowering plants, bamboo dustbins, 100% literacy, and a unique single living root bridge. It's near the Bangladesh border with sky views from a bamboo watchtower.
top_highlights: Single-decker living root bridge in village
how_to_reach_budget: Shared sumo Shillong to Dawki often stops at Mawlynnong. Direct sumo from Shillong ₹150, 3 hrs. Or hire from Dawki.
how_to_reach_private: Private cab from Shillong ₹2000-2500 for Dawki+Mawlynnong combo.
cultural_etiquette: Strictly zero littering — the whole village enforces it. Dispose of waste only in provided bins. Respect the community's pride in cleanliness.

name: Kaziranga National Park
tagline: Home of the Great One-Horned Rhinoceros
description: Kaziranga National Park is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and home to two-thirds of the world's one-horned rhinoceros population. The park also supports tigers, elephants, wild water buffalo, and swamp deer across its flood plains. Elephant and jeep safaris run November-April.
top_highlights: Jeep safari — rhino, elephant, tiger sightings
Kohora tourist village with local cuisine
how_to_reach_budget: ASTC bus from Guwahati to Kohora (Kaziranga gate) ₹150-200, 4-5 hrs. Or shared sumo ₹200-250.
how_to_reach_private: Private cab from Guwahati ₹2500-3500. Drive on NH27.
entry_fees: Indian: ₹100/person + jeep safari ₹2500 (shared, up to 6). Elephant safari: ₹900/person. Camera fee: ₹200
permit_info: No permit for Indian nationals. Foreign nationals: ₹650 entry + different rates.
cultural_etiquette: Park rules: no noise, no flash, stay in vehicle. Early morning safaris (6am) have best sightings. Book safaris in advance in peak season.

name: Majuli River Island
tagline: World's Largest River Island — Sattra Culture
description: Majuli is the world's largest inhabited river island on the Brahmaputra. It is the cultural and spiritual heart of Vaishnavite Assam, home to 22 Sattras (monasteries) practicing Sattriya dance and mask-making. The island is slowly eroding due to floods — visiting is both a joy and an act of witness.
top_highlights: Sattriya dance performance at a Sattra
Cycling between sattras on flat island roads
how_to_reach_budget: ASTC bus to Jorhat ₹200-300 from Guwahati, 5-6 hrs. Ferry from Nimati Ghat, Jorhat to Majuli ₹35-50 (1.5-2 hrs). Ferries run ~4-5 times daily.
how_to_reach_private: Private cab Guwahati to Jorhat ₹3500-4500. Same ferry.
entry_fees: Island entry: free; Sattra entry: usually free (donation welcome); ferry: ₹35-50
cultural_etiquette: Sattras are active monasteries — dress modestly, remove shoes, ask permission before photographing monks. The island is slowly sinking — treat it with reverence.

name: Tawang
tagline: India's Largest Buddhist Monastery at 10,000 ft
description: Tawang is home to the 400-year-old Tawang Monastery, the largest in India and second-largest in Asia. The town sits at 10,000 feet in the Himalayas near the China and Bhutan borders. The drive via Sela Pass (13,700 ft) is one of India's most dramatic. ILP is mandatory.
top_highlights: Sela Pass at 13,700 ft — often snow-covered
Bumla Pass at Indo-China border (PAP required)
how_to_reach_budget: Shared sumo from Tezpur to Tawang ₹600-800, 10-12 hrs (overnight or early morning). Via Bomdila and Sela Pass.
how_to_reach_private: Private cab from Guwahati ₹8000-12000, 2-day drive via Tezpur.
entry_fees: Monastery: ₹20; Museum: ₹20; Madhuri Lake: ₹100 vehicle entry
permit_info: ILP (Inner Line Permit) MANDATORY for all Indians — apply at arunachalilp.com or at Tezpur/Guwahati DC office. ₹100 fee. PAP required for foreign nationals (more restrictions).
cultural_etiquette: Tibetan Buddhist customs: circumambulate stupas clockwise, do not point feet at altars, ask before photography. Monks are active — be silent in prayer halls.
emergency_contact: Tawang District Hospital: 03794-222026; Army emergency via DC Office: 03794-222036

name: Dzukou Valley
tagline: Valley of Flowers — Nagaland's Hidden Alpine Paradise
best_season: June to September (flowers), December to January (snow)
description: Dzukou Valley is an alpine paradise straddling Nagaland and Manipur at 2,452m. In June-September it blazes with Dzukou lilies and rhododendrons. In winter it fills with snow. The 2-day trek from Viswema is one of Northeast India's finest — camping by the stream with zero light pollution.
top_highlights: Summit ridge views to Kohima and Manipur
how_to_reach_budget: Shared vehicle from Kohima to Viswema base camp ₹100-150. Trek start: Viswema or Jakhama gate. Porter hire ₹600-800/day.
how_to_reach_private: Private cab from Kohima ₹800-1000 to base. Same trek.
entry_fees: Forest entry: ₹100; camping permit: ₹50 per night at base camp
permit_info: No ILP for Nagaland. Carry ID. Restrict camping to designated areas.
cultural_etiquette: Naga tribal land — do not venture off trail. Carry out all trash. Campfire only in designated pits. Hire local guides/porters for economic benefit.
emergency_contact: Kohima District Hospital: 0370-2290246; Forest Range Office Viswema: 0370-2290073

name: Loktak Lake & Keibul Lamjao
description: Loktak is India's largest freshwater lake and contains Keibul Lamjao — the world's only floating national park, home to the endangered Sangai (brow-antlered deer). The lake's floating islands (phumdis) are unique in the world. Boat tours among phumdis are otherworldly.
top_highlights: Sangai deer sighting at Keibul Lamjao
how_to_reach_budget: Local bus from Imphal to Moirang ₹50-80, 1.5 hrs. Boat hire from Moirang ghat ₹300-500/boat.
how_to_reach_private: Private cab from Imphal ₹800-1200 day trip.
entry_fees: Keibul Lamjao NP: ₹25 Indian; Sendra Park: ₹20; boat hire: ₹300-500
permit_info: ILP required to enter Manipur (applies_to: indian). Obtain before entering state.
cultural_etiquette: Manipur ILP is strict — always carry it. Sangai sightings are rare; respect park rules. Photography of local fishermen — ask first.

name: Gangtok
best_season: March to May, October to December
description: Gangtok is Sikkim's orderly, plastic-free capital with stunning Kanchenjunga views on clear days. The MG Marg promenade is the city's heart. Rumtek Monastery, Tsomgo Lake, and Nathula Pass (India-China border) are nearby. Base for North Sikkim (Lachung/Yumthang) adventures.
top_highlights: MG Marg promenade — Sikkim's main street
Tsomgo Lake — alpine lake at 12,000 ft
Kanchenjunga dawn views from Tashi View Point
how_to_reach_budget: Shared jeep/sumo from Bagdogra (NJP) ₹200-300, 4-5 hrs. Helicopters (₹2500) also run Bagdogra-Gangtok.
entry_fees: MG Marg: free; Rumtek: ₹50; Tsomgo Lake: ₹200 vehicle + ₹25 person; Nathula: ₹200 Indian (PAP needed)
permit_info: No ILP for Gangtok. PAP required for Nathula Pass and North Sikkim (Lachung/Yumthang) — obtainable at Gangtok district office or through travel agent. Foreigners: PAP required for most areas beyond Gangtok.
cultural_etiquette: Sikkim bans plastic bags — carry cloth bag. Photography of army installations strictly prohibited. Remove shoes at monasteries.

name: Kohima
tagline: WWII History Meets Naga Warrior Culture
description: Kohima is the capital of Nagaland and site of the Battle of Kohima (1944) — a pivotal WWII turning point. The moving War Cemetery honors Allied soldiers. Nearby Hornbill Festival (December) showcases all 16 Naga tribes. Local Naga villages offer authentic cultural immersion.
top_highlights: Kohima War Cemetery — 'The Tennis Court' battle
how_to_reach_budget: ASTC/state bus from Guwahati ₹400-600, 8-10 hrs. Shared cab from Dimapur ₹150-200, 3 hrs (Dimapur is nearest railhead).
entry_fees: War Cemetery: free; Nagaland State Museum: ₹20; Hornbill Festival: ₹30-50/day
permit_info: No ILP for Nagaland. RAP/PAP needed for some border districts (not Kohima). Carry photo ID.
cultural_etiquette: War cemetery is a solemn memorial — maintain silence, no games. Naga villages: ask permission before entering homes or photographing. Hornbill Festival is one of India's most welcoming — enjoy with respect.

name: Aizawl
tagline: Mizoram's Cliffside Capital — Serene and Literate
description: Aizawl clings to dramatic ridges in the Mizoram hills. It is one of India's most literate and peaceful cities. The Mizo people are known for exceptional hospitality. The city has no bars but great food, scenic viewpoints, and the unique Mizo cultural traditions including Cheraw dance.
how_to_reach_budget: Fly to Lengpui Airport (AJL), 30 km away. State bus from airport ₹100. Shared cab ₹150-200. Inter-state buses from Silchar/Guwahati (long, 15+ hrs).
entry_fees: State Museum: ₹20; Durtlang: free; Vantawng Falls: ₹30
permit_info: ILP REQUIRED for all Indians visiting Mizoram. Obtainable at: Lengpui Airport on arrival, Aizawl checkpoint, or online. Bring two passport photos and ID.
cultural_etiquette: Mizo society is deeply Christian. Sundays are quiet — most shops closed. No alcohol sold (dry state). Hosts will offer food — accepting is a sign of respect. Dress modestly.
